key_insight: Patch Policy shows that dense patch-level visual features from pretrained Vision Transformers can improve embodied control by preserving fine-grained spatial detail without needing heavyweight models. It bridges the gap between efficient robot policies and the rich representations learned in large-scale vision pretraining.
problem_solved: Most robot policies either compress an image into one global token, losing spatial detail, or train visual backbones from scratch, missing the benefits of pretrained ViT features. This paper addresses the need for a lightweight policy that can use dense visual representations effectively for control.
method: Uses pretrained ViT patch features as dense inputs instead of a single global image embedding.
Designs an efficient policy architecture for embodied control that can exploit spatially detailed visual representations.
Avoids the computational cost of large vision-language-action models while retaining the advantages of dense visual pretraining.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a more data-efficient and spatially aware path to robot control. It may enable stronger embodied policies with lower training cost and better use of existing pretrained visual models.
